# plat.plus status

The status page of [plat.plus](https://plat.plus): **[status.plat.plus](https://status.plat.plus)**.

[Upptime](https://github.com/upptime/upptime) checks plat.plus regularly from GitHub's machines, so the checks and this page keep running when plat.plus is down. Each outage becomes an issue here. The page itself is plain HTML, rebuilt after every check (`page/`) and served from Hetzner in Germany, so visitors never reach GitHub.

## How it fits together

- `.upptimerc.yml`: the checked addresses.
- `.github/workflows/uptime.yml`, `response-time.yml`, `summary.yml`: Upptime's checks, copied from its template.
- `.github/workflows/page.yml`: builds `page/` into static files after each check and uploads them to Hetzner Webhosting S (Nuremberg) over FTPS; the secrets it needs are listed at its top. `page/htaccess` holds the web server rules (HTTPS, headers).
- Planned maintenance is an issue labelled `maintenance` with Upptime's comment (`start`, `end`, `expectedDown`). Upptime opens no outage for a service it names while the window runs; the page shows it apart from outages, coming ones and those of the last 90 days. An issue closed as "not planned" was called off and is left out.
- `.github/workflows/maintenance.yml` (`page/restart.mjs`): plat.plus's main server dispatches it when it schedules a restart for a security update, and again if the restart is cancelled. It opens or closes the matching maintenance issue (label `server-restart`), a 15-minute window from the restart time. Once the server's sites answer again, the server reports that moment (`done`), and the issue's end moves to it. The page lists past maintenance by start time and real length.
- `page/`: the page, without dependencies. `node page/build.mjs --fixture` renders sample data into `_site/`; `node --test "page/*.test.mjs"` runs the tests.
